text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; this is a medical emergency that requires immediate clarification. Can you tell me your exact age in hours or days, and are you passing any stool at all?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus. The combination of bilious vomiting in a six-hour-old newborn, especially with a family history of pyloric stenosis, is highly suggestive of this surgical emergency; the patient likely has not yet passed meconium, and immediate surgical consultation is required.
